title: 71-year-old man with progressive breathlessness
presenting_complaint: Progressive breathlessness over 5 days, now breathless at rest, with leg swelling and orthopnea.

history_items.question: Ask about orthopnea/PND
history_items.finding: Sleeping on 3 pillows now, woke gasping for air last night.
history_items.evidence_basis: Orthopnea/PND are classic decompensated heart-failure symptoms.

history_items.question: Ask about leg swelling
history_items.finding: Bilateral ankle swelling, worse over the past week.
history_items.evidence_basis: Peripheral edema is a congestion marker in heart failure.

history_items.question: Ask about prior cardiac history
history_items.finding: Had an MI 4 years ago, known reduced ejection fraction.
history_items.evidence_basis: Prior MI/known reduced EF strongly raises pretest probability of decompensated heart failure.

history_items.question: Ask about medication compliance and diet
history_items.finding: Ran out of furosemide 10 days ago; has been eating more salty food.

examination_items.finding: Raised JVP to the angle of the jaw.
examination_items.evidence_basis: Raised JVP is a core sign of volume overload.

investigations.name: BNP
investigations.result_detail: Markedly elevated, consistent with decompensated heart failure.
investigations.evidence_basis: BNP is a standard discriminator between cardiac and non-cardiac causes of dyspnea.

investigations.name: Chest X-ray
investigations.result_summary: Cardiomegaly, bilateral perihilar haziness, small effusions.
investigations.evidence_basis: Chest X-ray findings support the clinical diagnosis of congestion.

investigations.name: 12-lead ECG
investigations.result_summary: Old Q waves in the anterior leads, no acute ST changes.
investigations.result_detail: Evidence of prior infarction, no new ischemia.
investigations.evidence_basis: Useful background context but not discriminating for this presentation.

clinical_decisions.label: Treat as decompensated heart failure: IV diuretics, oxygen, fluid restriction, daily weights
clinical_decisions.rationale: Matches the congestive picture (raised JVP, crackles, edema, elevated BNP, known reduced EF).

clinical_decisions.label: Treat empirically as COPD exacerbation with bronchodilators and steroids
clinical_decisions.rationale: Ignores the congestive picture and history of reduced EF; would not address the underlying fluid overload.

outcome_branches.title: Appropriate decongestion
outcome_branches.narrative: The patient responds well to IV furosemide with a 3L net negative fluid balance over 48 hours, breathlessness resolves, and he is discharged on an optimized heart-failure regimen with follow-up.
outcome_branches.educational_explanation: Recognizing the congestive pattern (raised JVP, crackles, edema, elevated BNP) in a patient with known reduced EF and treating the fluid overload directly is the correct approach.

outcome_branches.title: Delayed decongestion
outcome_branches.narrative: Bronchodilators provide no benefit; the patient's oxygen saturation continues to fall overnight before the team reconsiders and starts diuretics 12 hours later than they could have.
outcome_branches.educational_explanation: Anchoring on a respiratory cause despite strong cardiac congestion signs delayed the correct, effective treatment.

counterfactual_branches.alternative_action_label: What if you had skipped BNP and gone straight on clinical impression?
counterfactual_branches.alternative_evidence: The exam findings alone (raised JVP, crackles, edema) already strongly suggest decompensated HF; BNP adds confirmatory confidence particularly useful if the picture were more mixed (e.g. co-existing COPD).
counterfactual_branches.probability_effect: Modest reduction in diagnostic certainty, more relevant in a less classic presentation than this one.
counterfactual_branches.potential_outcome: Likely the same correct management pathway here, but with less objective documentation to support it.
counterfactual_branches.reasoning_lesson: In a classic presentation, exam findings alone can be sufficient, but objective markers strengthen the case, especially with mixed cardiorespiratory pictures.

reasoning_error_catalog.label: Anchoring
reasoning_error_catalog.trigger: COPD chosen as leading differential despite raised JVP, crackles, edema, and elevated BNP all being available.
reasoning_error_catalog.educational_note: Fixating on a respiratory cause despite strong disconfirming cardiac signs.

reasoning_error_catalog.label: Ignoring red flags
reasoning_error_catalog.trigger: h_prior_mi or e_jvp not checked before the final decision.
reasoning_error_catalog.educational_note: Missing the background history/exam findings that most strongly point to a cardiac cause.

ml_feature_hint.note: See docs/DATASETS.md for the dataset's empirical (non-standard) cp/exang encoding used here.

references: Standard MBBS-level acute decompensated heart failure teaching pathway (congestion signs, BNP, CXR).
